description: We are a student team from Türkiye participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our project aims to develop health monitoring software for astronauts during space missions. We want to explore ways to monitor astronauts’ health and improve their safety in space. We are interested in science, technology, and space exploration. We welcome creative and motivated teammates with skills in coding, research, software, data analysis, and design. Let’s create something meaningful together!
summary:
HEALTH IN ZERO-G by Team VITARION proposes Smart Health Monitoring for Astronauts, an AI-powered system that protects crew health in space.

The problem: NASA’s five spaceflight hazards are space radiation (cancer risk, nervous system effects), isolation and confinement (sleep, mood and stress), distance from Earth (delayed communication, no quick evacuation), gravity fields (bone and muscle loss, fluid shifts) and hostile or closed environments (shared air, noise, tight space).

The solution: A smart wristband measures pulse, SpO₂, blood pressure, sleep and activity every five minutes, with more frequent checks when risk appears. AI builds each astronaut’s personal baseline and flags deviations. Three alert levels (info, alert, critical vibrating alarm) escalate to the medical team. Fingerprint access protects personal profiles.

A digital assistant takes symptoms via chat, weighs them against biometric data and health history, and gives guidance based on verified medical protocols. It never diagnoses; it supports doctors.

Safety: critical readings automatically alert the medical team and open a direct line to a doctor. Data is encrypted, access is authorized, and offline protocols work if contact with Earth is lost.

Message: early detection, rapid response, safe missions.

Sources: NASA HRP, NASA OCHMO Medical Technical Briefs, International Space Station, NASA’s The Human Body in Space.
